_readme: ENGLISH IS THE SCHEMA. Every other strings/<locale>.json is this file with the
same keys and translated values — build-i18n.mjs refuses to emit a locale whose
shape does not match. Keys are page.section.item and are STABLE: rename a key and
you throw away nine translations of it, so add a new one instead.
INLINE MARKUP. Most values are plain text. A value keeps HTML inside it only when
the sentence genuinely contains it — emphasis that has to move with the words, or
a link whose anchor text is part of the sentence. Three tags appear:
<strong>/<b>/<em>  emphasis. Move it to whatever words carry the stress in your
language; never delete it.
<a href="…">       a link. Translate the words, NEVER touch the href — the build
compares your opening tags against English and fails on a
changed URL. Locale prefixes are added by the build.
<mark>…</mark>     the words the hand-drawn ink stroke is drawn under. Exactly one
pair per value; the stroke itself is markup, not your problem.
a hard line break in a postal address.
Everything else — the SVG marks, layout, classes — lives in the HTML and never
reaches a translator.
PLACEHOLDERS. {name} in single braces is filled in at runtime (pricing only). Move
it inside the sentence, never rename it.
NOT HERE, ON PURPOSE: the language names in the switcher (each is written in its
own language, so it is never translated), the nine endonyms in the language pills,
brand and provider names, prices, and company/registration numbers.

leadership.title: See the school clearly
leadership.body: Live dashboards, an at-risk worklist, and an assistant that answers questions about your own data.

teachers.title: Teach, don't typeset
teachers.body: Full lesson kits from the school's own textbooks, plus each teacher's personal week and cover duties.

students.title: One place to learn
students.body: Assigned lessons that play in class or at home, worksheets to hand in, and a tutor that sticks to the chapter.

parents.title: Finally in the loop
parents.body: Each child's assignments, scores and due dates — read-only, and only for their own children.

leadership.heading: Answers, not spreadsheets.
leadership.sub: Everything a principal's office asks for on a Monday morning — already computed, already scoped to who's asking.

analytics.title: The at-risk list writes itself
analytics.body: Whole-school activity, completion and overdue work at a glance. Students who go quiet, slip or fall behind are flagged by rule — coordinators get a named, actionable worklist; principals see clean aggregates by grade.

briefing.title: Ask the school a question
briefing.body: A briefing assistant that answers from your school's live numbers only — "which Grade 5 students need a call home this week?" — with every briefing recorded in the access log.

support.title: Spot who needs backup
support.body: Each teacher's lessons, assignments and grading backlog next to their classes' progress — framed as support flags, not rankings, so help arrives before burnout does.

governance.title: Who sees what, in writing
governance.body: A plain-language access page states exactly what every role can see, coordinators get scoped grants (their grades, nothing more), and leadership views land in an audit log.

timetable.heading: A week that builds itself — and covers itself.
timetable.sub: Set your start time, period length and breaks. SketchCast fills the rest, and keeps it standing when someone calls in sick.

generate.title: Good rules, applied everywhere
generate.body: The class teacher opens every day, core subjects run daily for every class, enrichment fills the gaps with variety — and no teacher is ever double-booked or pushed past their daily cap.

editable.title: Your judgement wins
editable.body: Drag to move or swap, lock the cells the generator must never touch, copy or clear a day, undo anything. Period times are derived from your start time and breaks — change one number, the whole day shifts.

cover.title: Absent at 7:02, covered by 7:03
cover.body: Mark a teacher absent and every lesson gets a cover plan — subject teacher first, then class teacher, then the lightest load, only from staff with room in their day. No cover available? It says so, honestly.

personal.title: Everyone knows where to be
personal.body: Every teacher sees their own week and any cover duties from their own login; every student sees their class grid, breaks and times included.

lessons.heading: Your textbooks, taught.
lessons.sub: The same engine individual teachers love, at school scale: upload the books your school actually teaches from, and every chapter becomes a complete kit.

kit.title: Six pieces, one click
kit.body: Every generate produces the complete kit together — a narrated video lesson that draws itself, an editable deck, a lesson plan, activities, a worksheet and an exam paper — grounded in the chapter, not the internet.

parts.title: Parts, not marathons
parts.body: Long chapters split into classroom-sized parts — each with its own video and kit, generated on demand, so a 40-page chapter becomes four teachable lessons.

languages.title: Taught in your language
languages.body: The book's language is detected automatically, and lessons narrate in a matching voice — including fully mirrored right-to-left Arabic.

assign.title: From generated to graded
assign.body: Assign any item to a class with a due date; submissions come back auto-scored with the teacher's mark on top — the same records leadership analytics read.

coach.title: A tutor that stays on the page
coach.body: Students on school plans get Ask Coach: a tutor locked to the assigned chapter — it explains, quizzes and recaps from the book, never from outside it.

health.title: Bad scans flagged early
health.body: Every uploaded book gets a health score at indexing — text quality, structure, detected problems — so quality issues surface before a teacher builds a week on them.

parents.heading: The report card, every day.
parents.sub: Parents join by school invitation, already linked to their own children — nothing to set up, nothing extra to see.

progress.title: Each child, at a glance
progress.body: Assignments, completion, scores and overdue flags per child — read-only, scoped to their own children and no one else's.

calendar.title: School dates where families look
calendar.body: School events and class dates, subscribable into Google, Outlook or Apple calendars — with assignment deadlines riding along on the in-app calendar.

invitations.title: Invited, not registered
invitations.body: The school issues each parent invite with the child link already attached — so access is granted deliberately, never self-claimed.

practical.title: Small things, handled
practical.body: Forgot passwords stay in the family: a parent resets their own child's login and hands over a one-time password that must be changed at next sign-in.

trust.heading: Built for schools that answer to parents.

isolation.title: Walls in the database
isolation.body: Every read is scoped by role at the database layer — a student sees their own work, a teacher their classes, a coordinator their grades. The URL never decides.

audit.title: Leadership access, logged
audit.body: Every leadership view of student data — dashboards and briefings alike — is written to an access log the school admin can read.

provisioning.body: Teacher and admin accounts are provisioned with SketchCast staff, not self-served — rosters stay deliberate, licensing stays predictable.

support.title: Reports come back answered

Teaching at home — or tutoring across four different schools — you get the book and nothing else. So every explanation, every practice sheet and every test gets built by one person, usually late at night, subject after subject.

faq.heading: Questions from homeschool families and tutors

q1.q: Can I use my own curriculum books?
q1.a: Yes — that is the point. Upload the book you already teach from as a single PDF. Photographed pages work too once combined into one PDF — the built-in page scanner turns your phone's photos into exactly that. Every lesson, worksheet and test paper is generated from that book's own chapters, so the material matches the syllabus your learner actually follows.

q2.q: How many children or students can I teach on one plan?
q2.a: Home Basic covers up to 2 learners; Homeschool covers up to 10. Each learner has their own login, their own books and their own progress record — enough for a big homeschooling family, or a tutor's full student roster.

q3.q: Which languages does it work in?
q3.a: Lessons are generated in 9 languages, auto-detected from the book you upload — including Arabic, fully right-to-left on slides and worksheets. You teach in the language of your book, not the language of our website.

q4.q: Do I get records for my homeschool portfolio or review?
q4.a: Yes. Everything taught, assigned and completed is recorded as you go, and one button exports a printable report per learner: chapters covered per subject, work completed and assessment results, with dates. Families use it for portfolio reviews; tutors send the same report as the monthly parent update.

q5.q: Can a tutor use it with students from different schools?
q5.a: Yes. Each student keeps their own books, so you can upload each student's own school textbook and generate practice papers against that student's actual syllabus. Six students from four schools is a normal setup here.

q6.a: You can start free with one complete lesson kit — no card needed. Home Basic is $9.99 a month for a subject or two, and Homeschool is $34 a month or $340 a year (two months free) for the whole curriculum: 48 generations a month, up to 10 learners and printable progress records.

cta.sub: Upload one chapter and get the full six-piece kit free — no card, no trial timer. If it saves you an evening, the plans are there.
cta.note: Questions about homeschooling or tuition use? Talk to us — a real person answers.

meta.title: Privacy Policy — SketchCast AI
meta.description: How SketchCast AI collects, uses, and protects data — including how we protect students.

privacy.intro1: SketchCast AI (“SketchCast”, “we”, “us”, “our”) turns textbook chapters into narrated lessons, decks, videos, worksheets, and an optional book-grounded AI study assistant, for schools, teachers, parents, and their students. Many of our users are children, so we hold ourselves to a simple standard: collect the minimum, use it only to teach, never sell it, never advertise with it, never use it to train AI models, and never track behaviour for any purpose other than showing teachers and parents learning progress.
privacy.intro2: This policy explains what we collect, why, who we share it with, how long we keep it, and the rights you have. It applies to sketchcast.app and app.sketchcast.app.

toc.label: On this page:
toc.items: 1. Who we are · 2. Which laws apply · 3. What we collect · 4. Children’s privacy & the school’s role · 5. How we use data & our legal bases · 6. AI processing · 7. Who processes data for us (sub-processors) · 8. International transfers · 9. Cookies & tracking · 10. Retention & deletion · 11. Security & breach notification · 12. Your rights · 13. Automated processing · 14. Schools (DPA) · 15. Changes & contact

s1.p1: The service is operated by Aethel Twin Sdn. Bhd., Registration No. 202601012908 (1675006-X), a company incorporated in Malaysia (“the operator”), registered at D-1-1, Bangi Gateway Shopping Complex, Persiaran Pekeliling, Seksyen 15, 43650 Bandar Baru Bangi, Selangor, Malaysia. For the personal data described here, the operator is the data controller / data fiduciary — except for data inside a school’s workspace, where the school is the controller and we act as its processor under our agreement with the school (see §14).
s1.p2: Privacy contact / grievance officer: reachable at privacy@sketchcast.app (or hello@sketchcast.app), tel +60 11-2088 2016. We aim to acknowledge requests within 72 hours and to resolve them within the timeframes set by applicable law.

s2.p1: SketchCast is available in more than one country, so the protections you can rely on depend on where you and your school are. Wherever you are, the commitments above apply. In addition:
s2.li1: India — the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act), including its provisions for children’s data and verifiable parental consent.
s2.li2: European Economic Area & United Kingdom — the GDPR / UK GDPR, including the rules on children’s consent and on transfers outside the EEA/UK.
s2.li3: United States — where a US school uses SketchCast, the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) — under which the school provides consent on parents’ behalf for the limited educational purpose here — and the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA), under which we act as a “school official” with a legitimate educational interest and use student records only as the school directs.
s2.li4: California — the CCPA/CPRA. We do not “sell” or “share” personal information as those terms are defined, and we honour the additional protections for consumers under 16.
s2.p2: If a mandatory local law gives you stronger rights than this policy describes, that law prevails.

s3.adultsH: Teachers, parents, school admins, and coordinators (adults)
s3.adultsP: Name, email address, password (stored only as a salted hash by our authentication provider) or Google sign-in identity, role, and — for school staff — school affiliation. At sign-up we also collect a short profile you provide (e.g. the grades/subjects you teach, or, for a parent, how many children you support and their grade levels).
s3.studentsP: Student accounts are created by a teacher, parent, or school — students never sign themselves up. For each student we store: name, a login ID, a parent/guardian email address (used for account communication only), class enrolment, and learning records — which lessons were assigned, completion status, quiz/worksheet answers and scores, any answer files the student submits, and — if the AI study assistant is used — the messages the student types to it and its replies (see §6). Where a school or family uses the diary, we also store the notes teachers and parents write about the student, any replies the student writes, and a record of which parent acknowledged which note and when.
s3.healthH: Health & wellbeing notes in the diary
s3.healthP: The diary lets a parent or teacher record a note about a child's health or wellbeing — an absence, medication, an allergy, or a concern — so the adults teaching that child can act on it. We treat this as sensitive information: it is provided at the parent's or school's initiative, it is visible only to that child's teachers, their parents and their school's leadership, and it is never used for advertising and never used to train AI models. It is deleted with the student's record, and the author can delete it at any time. Please don't use the diary for medical emergencies — contact the school directly.
s3.contentP: Textbook chapters and materials teachers/parents upload, and the lessons, decks, videos, and worksheets we generate from them.
s3.paymentP: If you buy a paid plan, our payment providers (see §7) collect and process your payment details. We do not receive or store full card numbers. We store only your plan, billing status, and a provider reference needed to manage the subscription.
s3.technicalP: To keep the service running and secure we process basic technical data such as IP address, device/browser type, and error logs. We use no advertising or analytics trackers, no behavioural-profiling SDKs, and no cookies other than the session cookie that keeps you signed in. We do not collect student phone numbers, home addresses, photos, biometrics, or precise location.

s4.li1: Student accounts exist only inside a school’s, teacher’s, or parent’s workspace and are created, named, and managed by that adult — acting with the parental consent required by applicable law (e.g. the DPDP Act, GDPR Art. 8, or COPPA’s school-consent mechanism).
s4.li2: Student data is used for exactly one purpose: delivering assigned lessons and showing the student’s own teachers, school, and parent how learning is going. We apply data minimisation — we ask for no more student data than that purpose needs.
s4.li3: We never advertise to students, never sell or share student data for commercial purposes, and never use student data (including AI-assistant conversations) to train AI models.
s4.li4: Access to student data is role-scoped: a teacher sees only their own classes; a coordinator sees only the grades assigned to them; a parent sees only their own children; leadership views of student-level data are recorded in an access log the school admin can review.
s4.li5: Parents or guardians may review, correct, or request deletion of their child’s data at any time — through the school/teacher, or directly at the contact in §1 — and may withdraw consent, which ends further processing of that child’s data.

s5.h: 5. How we use data & our legal bases
s5.li1: To run the service — sign-in, generating teaching materials, assigning them, the AI study assistant, and recording progress and grades for the student’s own teachers, school, and parent. Basis: performance of our contract with you (or, for student data, the school’s instructions and consent).
s5.li2: To communicate about accounts — e.g. sending login credentials to a parent’s email, password resets, and service notices. Basis: contract / legitimate interests.
s5.li3: To keep the service secure, prevent abuse, and debug failures. Basis: legitimate interests / legal obligation.
s5.li4: To take payment for paid plans. Basis: contract.
s5.p: We do not use your data for advertising, and we do not sell it to anyone. Where we rely on consent (e.g. a child’s data, or premium voices), you may withdraw it at any time.

s6.p1: SketchCast uses artificial intelligence in two ways, and we are precise about what is sent where:
s6.li1: Generating lessons. The uploaded chapter content is sent to Anthropic (Claude) to produce the lesson, deck, worksheet, and exam; the lesson script text is sent to Microsoft (Edge text-to-speech) or — only when a school enables premium voices — ElevenLabs, to produce narration. This step does not send student personal data.
s6.li2: The AI study assistant. When a teacher, parent, or student uses the optional assistant, the questions they type are sent to Anthropic (Claude), together with the relevant book/lesson content, so it can answer. This means a student’s typed messages are processed by our AI provider. A short constrained maths service (self-hosted) may also be called to check calculations. We store the assistant conversation for up to 30 days so the student can continue where they left off, and to let you review it.
s6.li3: Translating diary notes. When a reader taps “Translate” on a diary note, the text of that note and its replies is sent to Anthropic (Claude) to translate it into the chosen language, and the translation is stored so it never has to be produced twice. Only the message text is sent — no names, account ids or school details are attached — though a note written by a teacher or parent may of course mention a child by name. Anyone who can read a note can translate it, including the student.
s6.p2: Our AI providers process this content only to provide the service. Under their business terms they do not use it to train their models and are not permitted to use it for advertising. We do not use your content or your students’ data to train any AI model. The assistant is grounded in the book and is designed to give hints and method — not graded answers — but, like all AI, its output can contain errors and should be reviewed.

s7.p1: We use a small number of vetted providers to run the service. Each processes data only on our instructions and under a data-processing agreement.
s7.railway: Runs the lesson-generation worker and maths service
s7.anthropic: AI generation, the study assistant, and diary translation (§6)
s7.tts: Narration audio (ElevenLabs only when premium voices are enabled)
s7.google: Optional “Sign in with Google” for adult accounts only
s7.lemonSqueezy: Payments for parent/teacher plans (as Merchant of Record)
s7.p2: We will keep this list current and give schools notice of material changes to sub-processors that handle student data before they take effect.

s8.p: Some of the providers above are based in, or process data in, the United States and other countries outside your own. Where we transfer personal data across borders, we rely on appropriate safeguards — such as the European Commission’s Standard Contractual Clauses (and the UK Addendum), the providers’ own compliance commitments, and, for student data, the school’s instructions. You can ask us for details of the safeguards that apply to a given transfer.

s9.p: We use a single essential cookie — the session cookie that keeps you signed in. We do not use advertising cookies, analytics cookies, cross-site trackers, or “Do Not Track”-defeating techniques. Because we use only an essential cookie, no cookie-consent banner is required, but you can clear the cookie at any time by signing out.

s10.li1: Account data is kept for as long as the account is active.
s10.li2: Uploaded books and generated content are kept until you delete them — teachers/parents can delete them at any time in the product.
s10.li3: Student learning records are deleted when the student is removed; removing a student deletes their profile and records with them.
s10.li4: AI-assistant conversations are kept for up to 30 days, then deleted.
s10.li5: Diary notes, replies and acknowledgments are kept while the account is active and are deleted with the student's record. The author of a note or reply can delete it at any time; deleting a note also deletes its replies, the acknowledgments on it, and any stored translations of it.
s10.li6: Technical logs are kept for a short period (typically up to 90 days) for security and debugging, then deleted or anonymised.
s10.li7: To close an account or delete a school’s data entirely, email us — we complete deletion within 30 days, except where law requires longer retention (e.g. tax records of a payment). Backups are overwritten on a rolling cycle.

s11.p1: Data is encrypted in transit; passwords are hashed; every database query is scoped by row-level security so users reach only data their role permits; files are served through short-lived signed links; leadership access to student-level data is audit-logged; payment card details never touch our servers. No system is perfectly secure, but minimal collection is our first protection — what we don’t hold can’t leak.
s11.p2: If a personal-data breach occurs that is likely to create a risk to you, we will notify the relevant supervisory authority and affected schools/users without undue delay and within the timeframes required by applicable law, and describe what happened and what we are doing about it.

s12.p1: Subject to your local law, you have the right to: access the personal data we hold about you; correct it; delete it; obtain a copy in a portable format; restrict or object to certain processing; and withdraw consent where we rely on it. Parents and guardians may exercise these rights for their child. We do not discriminate against you for exercising them, and we will not sell or share your data.
s12.p2: To exercise a right, contact us at the address in §1 — if you are part of a school, your school admin can also action most requests directly in the product. If you believe we have mishandled your data, you may lodge a complaint with your local data-protection authority (for example, the Data Protection Board of India, an EU/EEA supervisory authority, the UK ICO, or the California Privacy Protection Agency).

s13.p: Some features compute helpful signals automatically — for example a “book health” quality score at upload, an at-risk learning worklist for teachers, and auto-scoring of objective quiz questions. These assist a teacher’s judgment and are always reviewable and overridable by a human; we do not make decisions producing legal or similarly significant effects about a student by automated means alone. AI-generated teaching materials should always be reviewed by a teacher before classroom use.

s14.h: 14. Schools: our role & a data-processing agreement
s14.p: When a school uses SketchCast, the school is the controller of its students’ data and we are its processor: we process student data only on the school’s documented instructions, for the educational purpose, and under confidentiality. Schools that need a formal Data Processing Addendum (DPA) — including sub-processor terms and, where relevant, Standard Contractual Clauses — can request one at the contact in §1.

s15.p: If we change this policy, we will update this page and its “Last updated” date, and notify schools of any material change affecting student data before it takes effect. Questions or requests: privacy@sketchcast.app.

To the maximum extent permitted by law, our total liability for any claim relating to the service is limited to the amount you paid us in the twelve months before the claim (or RM 100 if you paid nothing). Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited by law.

s8.p: You may stop using the service and request deletion at any time. We may suspend or close accounts that violate these terms. Schools may export their materials before closure by downloading them from the dashboard.

s9.p: These terms are governed by the laws of Malaysia, and disputes are subject to the courts of Selangor, Malaysia.
